content: 1. Take this medication exactly as directed by your doctor, and share any results or concerns with them. 2. While using this medication, changes in body fat distribution may occur, such as increased fat in the upper back and abdominal areas or decreased fat in the arms and legs. The cause and long-term effects of these changes are not yet fully understood. 3. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. 4. This document does not list all potential side effects. If you are in the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. If you are in Canada, do the same. 5. Before starting nelfinavir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. 6. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. 7. If you are pregnant, inform your doctor before using this medication. Treatment with this medication can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby. 8. This medication passes into breast milk and may have undesirable effects on a nursing infant. Breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication, as breast milk can also transmit HIV. 9. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. 10. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. 11. Nelfinavir can slow the removal of other medications from your body, potentially affecting how they work. Similarly, other medications can affect the removal of nelfinavir, altering its effectiveness. 12. Examples of drugs that may interact with nelfinavir include apalutamide, certain anti-seizure drugs (e.g., carbamazepine, phenobarbital, primidone), and rifampin. 13. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods while on this medication. 14. In case of an overdose with serious symptoms like passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. 15. Regular lab and medical tests (e.g., liver function, viral load, T-cell counts, triglycerides/cholesterol, blood sugar) should be conducted while taking this medication. Keep all medical and lab appointments. 16. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. 17. Store this medication in its original container at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. 18. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. 19. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. 20. Diarrhea is a common side effect of this medication. If you experience diarrhea, ask your doctor or pharmacist about ways to manage it, such as using anti-diarrhea medication. 21. Nausea or gas may also occur. 22. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits to you outweigh the risks of side effects. 23. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off infections you already had, potentially causing disease symptoms to reappear. 24. Symptoms may also occur if your immune system becomes overactive. This reaction can happen at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or months later. 25. This medication may rarely cause an increase in blood sugar levels, which can lead to or worsen diabetes. Inform your doctor immediately if you experience symptoms of high blood sugar, such as increased thirst or urination. 26. If you already have diabetes, monitor your blood sugar levels regularly as directed and share the results with your doctor. 27. Changes in body fat distribution may occur while taking this medication, such as increased fat in the upper back and stomach areas or decreased fat in the arms and legs. The cause and long-term effects of these changes are unknown. 28. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. 29. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. If you are in the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. If you are in Canada, do the same.
